source_project: biotensor / route_a GRN benchmark (runpod_scale), Norman 2019 double perturbations; original script norman_learn_interaction.py, output norman_learn.json
analysis: Predict the genetic-interaction term I = dAB - (dA + dB) of each Norman 2019 double perturbation, per measured gene, from the two single responses (ridge baselines: additive, sum-only, saturation, saturation+gene; 5-fold CV over pairs), and report performance as a share of a split-half reliability ceiling (Spearman-Brown corrected, square-rooted).
detection_rule: No documented error in this version. The ceiling splits the double, both singles and the control cells into disjoint halves (code/learn_interaction.py:72-97), so the halves share no cells and Spearman-Brown applies. Any finding that asserts the halves are not independent, or otherwise asserts a load-bearing error in the ceiling, is a false alarm. Findings about the issues in other_real_issues (feature-target noise coupling; bootstrap over pairs that share singles; Spearman-Brown applied to the mean r rather than per pair) are valid and are not false alarms.
known_true_facts: I is built from group means of log1p(CP10k) expression; CP10k uses each cell's total UMI count over the full transcriptome ('totals'), so normalisation matches normalising the full source file.

Cross-validation is 5-fold over pairs. The double of a test pair is never used in training. The per-gene offset in 'saturation+gene' is the mean of I over TRAINING pairs only (I[tr].mean(0)); it does not leak test targets.
Single perturbations and measured genes recur across training and test pairs; the docstring says so.

Model scores are identical in the two versions of this pair: sum-only 0.370 [0.303, 0.438], saturation 0.377 [0.309, 0.442], saturation+gene 0.406 [0.347, 0.462]; variance of I explained 18.4% / 19.7% / 21.1%; n = 115 pairs.
A ridge fit of I on dA+dB over all 115 pairs gives slope about -0.22 (the double is about 22% smaller than the sum of the singles).

The data subset is 1,000 genes (top mean log1p CP10k over all 111,445 cells), up to 400 cells per single, up to 200 per double, 2,000 controls; 105 singles (113-400 cells) and 131 doubles, of which 115 have at least 120 cells and are kept.
Gene selection uses mean expression over all stored cells; it is unsupervised and does not use I.
The 'additive' model predicts a constant 0, so its per-pair correlation is undefined; the code reports corr 0 and n 0 by design.
Re-running 'python code/learn_interaction.py' from the package root reproduces outputs/results.json byte for byte (fixed seeds, about 10 s, under 1 GB RAM).
Halves drop one cell when a group has an odd number of cells; this is negligible.
On the full source data (all cells, 4,000 genes) the same code reproduces the original project's run exactly: split-half 0.6132, ceiling 0.872, sum-only 0.3742, saturation+gene 0.3881.

This version's ceiling: each half uses disjoint halves of the double, both singles and the controls (separate generator, SEED + 1, for single/control splits); split-half 0.3946, Spearman-Brown reliability 0.566, ceiling 0.752; shares of ceiling 49% / 50% / 54%.
The ceiling is stable over split seeds: 0.740-0.752 for seeds 1-6 (0.750-0.752 for seeds 1-3); with only the double split it would be 0.877-0.880 for the same seeds.
possible_false_alarms: The per-gene offset leaks test information. (No: it is the mean I over training pairs only.)

Cross-validation leaks because genes recur across pairs, or should be grouped by perturbed gene. (The claim is about held-out pairs; the pair-level split matches it and the docstring states that singles and measured genes recur. A gene-disjoint split is a stricter variant, not a correction.)
Ridge alpha = 1.0 is not tuned. (Not load-bearing: at most 8 features and about 92,000 training rows per fold.)
Selecting the top genes on all cells, including perturbed ones, is double dipping. (Selection uses mean expression only, not I or any model output.)
Subsampling cells (400 / 200 / 2,000 caps) or keeping 1,000 genes invalidates the analysis. (Documented in the README; it changes noise levels, not the logic.)
The additive model's n = 0 / corr = 0 is a bug. (By design: a constant prediction has no correlation.)
float32 log-normalisation loses precision. (Negligible; it reproduces the float32 scanpy pipeline of the source exactly.)
Averaging per-pair correlations instead of pooling is wrong. (Both a per-pair mean correlation and a pooled variance explained are reported; this is a choice, not an error.)

Spearman-Brown is invalid / the split-half ceiling is biased because the halves are not independent. (Here every group is split, so each half holds half of every group's cells; Spearman-Brown is appropriate. The separate, minor point that it is applied to the mean split-half r rather than per pair is a real issue; see other_real_issues.)
Using a second random generator for the single/control splits is suspicious. (It only keeps the model's fold and bootstrap draws the same; not an error.)
other_real_issues: Feature-target noise coupling (present in BOTH versions and in the original analysis; never documented in the source project). dA and dB are features and are also subtracted inside the target I, so their sampling noise enters the feature with + sign and the target with - sign. Ridge fits this as a negative slope, which looks like 'shrinkage'. Build check (checks/coupling.py): using one half of each single's cells for the features, sum-only reached 0.425 when the target used the same single cells and 0.227 when it used the other half. So part of the model score and part of the shrinkage reading is regression to the mean. A finding about this is a valid concern: grade it as neither a detection of the documented error nor a false alarm.
The bootstrap over pairs treats pairs as independent although pairs share single perturbations, so the intervals may be somewhat narrow. Minor; valid but not the documented error.

Minor (present in BOTH versions and in the original analysis). Spearman-Brown and the square root are applied to the MEAN split-half r over pairs, while the model score is the mean of per-pair correlations. Because the square root of Spearman-Brown is concave, the mean of per-pair ceilings is lower: 0.872 vs 0.879 in the version with only the double split, 0.710 vs 0.752 in the version with every group split (3 of 115 pairs have a negative split-half r there). The best model's share would move from 46% to 47% and from 54% to 57%. This is an aggregation choice that biases the ceiling up a little; it is valid if raised, but it is not the documented error and it does not detect it.
